case.background: A fixed amount of air is trapped above mercury in the sealed arm of a J-shaped tube. Add mercury pressure while holding the thermal condition fixed, then infer how pressure and air volume are related.
initial_observations: Adding mercury compresses the trapped air reversibly.
The bath prevents deliberate temperature changes during a run.

controls.description: Additional pressure applied by the mercury column above ambient.
controls.name: added_pressure_kpa

controls.description: Condition of the surrounding bath during compression.
controls.name: thermal_condition

instruments.description: A sealed J-shaped tube with trapped air, mercury, a volume scale, and an ambient-pressure reference.
instruments.name: sealed_j_tube

notes: The trapped amount of air and its temperature remain fixed.
Any non-empty subset of the two listed readouts may be requested.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'boyle_inverse_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain the following evaluator-required keys, spelled exactly: reference_volume_ml, ambient_pressure_kpa, and pressure_exponent.
For scoring, encode V = reference_volume_ml * ((ambient_pressure_kpa + added_pressure_kpa) / ambient_pressure_kpa)^pressure_exponent.

readouts.description: Volume of the trapped air column.
readouts.name: air_volume_ml

readouts.description: Absolute pressure of the trapped air.
readouts.name: absolute_pressure_kpa

case.title: Identify the isothermal pressure-volume response
